processes.description: Schedulers and pipeline account staff compare measured against scheduled or confirmed volumes at meters and interconnects, find where actuals did not come in as scheduled, and agree with the pipeline or counterparty how the imbalance is cleared: lending or parking gas, shifting nominations, paying back volumes in kind, or making manual book entries when the system cannot clear it. Rounds trade spreadsheets, OBA imbalance reports and volume statements, and ask the other side to verify or update contract and meter lists.
steps: A scheduler or the pipeline notices that actual volumes at a meter or contract differ from scheduled or confirmed volumes.
Staff pull measured versus scheduled volumes and prepare a spreadsheet or imbalance report by contract.
The report or a list of meters and contracts goes to the counterparty or pipeline to verify, add or update.
Both sides compare their numbers and request statements to support any volume differences by month.
The parties agree how to clear the imbalance: lend or park gas, adjust nominations, or pay back volumes.
Where the system cannot clear it, accounting makes manual entries to clear the imbalance from the books.

stalls.summary: Rounds wait on the other party: the Hub sends park and loan information late, a counterparty has no answer yet on why actuals differed, and an expected wire transfer is chased for over a week.

Requests arrive without a clear owner: a responder is unsure why Settlements is asking about imbalance deals, and another notes nobody with sign-off authority sits on the work, so papers are walked over by hand.
The scheduling system cannot clear some imbalances, so they recur monthly on the parking and lending contract and need manual book entries.
Reconciliations with pipelines run long and get chased, with reports rerun for older months after the other side reconciles.

contradictions.summary: Two people name different owners of the daily imbalance check: one says it has been Bill's since the reorg, while Bill says Darron has owned it since March.

automation.approach: A scheduled report that pulls measured and scheduled volumes per meter, contract and interconnect, flags differences beyond a tolerance, and produces the reconciliation spreadsheet and supporting statements by month, plus a written procedure naming the owner of the daily imbalance check and the steps for clearing imbalances the system cannot clear.
automation.rationale: The mail shows the same reconciliation spreadsheets rebuilt by hand and confusion over who owns the daily check and who signs off. A written procedure that fixes ownership, sign-off and the manual-entry path addresses the stalls directly, while the comparison report takes over the volume pulling.

work_estimate.rationale: Most of a round goes to pulling measured versus scheduled volumes, comparing them with the counterparty's figures, building the reconciliation spreadsheet and adjusting nominations or making manual entries. Simple meter shortfalls take little time; multi-month OBA reconciliations with statements take far longer, hence the wide range. Volume pulling and comparison is the automatable part; agreeing the payback stays manual.

processes.description: A desk coordinator records the origination recognized on deals each night, checks it against what was granted to each originating group, and follows up when amounts are missing from the schedule or a group claims more than it was granted. New groups are added to the origination file and given a daily report, and the coordinator asks who should grant origination on a given deal.
steps: Origination recognized on the night's deals is totalled.
The total is compared with what each originating group was granted.
Missing or over-claimed amounts are raised with the group or the person granting origination.
New groups' deals are added to the origination file and set up for a daily report.
The schedule and report are corrected once the amounts are confirmed.

stalls.summary: An origination amount expected from another party does not appear, leaving the schedule incomplete until it is chased.

contradictions.summary: A group's claimed origination does not match what was granted to it, so the two records disagree until reconciled.

automation.approach: A template origination schedule that lists each deal, the group granted origination, the amount granted and the amount claimed or recognized, with a check column flagging differences and missing grants for follow-up.
automation.rationale: The work is matching recognized and claimed origination against grants deal by deal; a shared schedule layout with a difference check makes gaps and over-claims visible without rebuilding the comparison each night.

processes.description: Gas control or a connected pipeline announces planned maintenance, pigging, tie-ins, turbine work or an unplanned leak repair. Logistics staff identify the meters in the affected section, notify the desk and producers or customers whose meters will be shut in or curtailed, and arrange how the gas is handled: holding it and batching it later, rescheduling, or deciding what to do when an outage is postponed. Some rounds need a notification letter to shippers.
steps: Gas control or a connected pipeline announces planned or emergency work on a section, plant or station.
Staff identify the meters in the affected section, checking the list against the pipeline's records.
The desk and affected producers or customers are notified of the shut-in or reduced capacity and its dates.
Counterparties agree how volumes are handled, such as holding gas and batching it later.
Notification letters are drafted where shippers must be formally informed.
Updates on postponements or extended outages are passed along until the work is complete.

stalls.summary: Rounds wait on replies from counterparties or colleagues: a call about a notification letter goes unanswered, and the desk presses for a quick response on how line work will affect deliveries.
Outages shift after notice goes out, so planned outages are postponed or extended and the desk has to decide again what to do with the affected days.

automation.approach: A reusable maintenance notice that takes the section, dates and affected meter list from the pipeline's records and goes to a standing distribution of the desk and affected producers and customers, with fields for expected volume impact, the handling arrangement and any postponement update.
automation.rationale: Most rounds are the same announcement re-sent with a new meter list and dates; a standard notice with the meter list drawn from the system cuts the retyping and makes postponements easy to reissue, while staff still agree how volumes are handled.

work_estimate.rationale: A round mainly involves looking up the meters in the affected section, checking them against the pipeline's records, and arranging how the gas is handled with producers or customers. Most notices are short and routine; rounds needing a shipper notification letter or rearranged deliveries take longer. The meter lookup and notice are the automatable part.
